subject: Urban Planning
title: Setbacks and Lot Coverage: The Invisible Rules
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Setbacks and Lot Coverage: The Invisible Rules.

hook.text: Zoning says your house must sit 25 feet from the street, 10 feet from neighbors, and cover only 40% of the lot.

buildup.text: Setbacks create the suburban look: houses centered on large lots surrounded by empty grass on all sides.

discovery.text: These rules prevent the tight-knit rowhouse blocks of Brooklyn or Georgetown — homes built to the lot line.

twist.text: Front setbacks were originally for future road widening. The roads were never widened. The setbacks remain.

climax.text: Reducing setbacks and increasing lot coverage lets the same lot hold twice the housing — without going taller.

punchline.text: The grass between your house and the street? Zoning put it there. Not your choice.

quiz.question: What was the original purpose of front setbacks in zoning?
options: Ensuring every home had a front garden for aesthetics
Reserving space for future road widening projects
Reducing fire spread between neighboring properties
